text:
ConocoPhillips gained a modest 0.23% today, continuing a stronger two-week rally of 6%. The stock has climbed steadily since early September as oil prices surged above $100 a barrel on Middle East tensions—Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was shut down following drone attacks, and Iran-U.S. conflict risks have kept crude elevated. The company benefits directly when crude prices rise, since higher oil prices increase the value of the oil it produces and sells.

Today's small gain reflects some pullback in oil prices on Friday as markets briefly priced in hopes for peace talks, but crude remains well above $95 and the two-week trend shows investors see lasting support from regional instability. The gap between U.S. oil ($97) and global oil prices ($110) also suggests continued tight supply concerns that favor major producers like ConocoPhillips.
